findings.title: Increment retryCount atomically instead of writing a stale value
findings.body: Both failure paths set retryCount to the value fetched at the beginning of the cron run plus one. If two cron requests overlap and both fail to schedule the same reminder, they read the same count and overwrite each other, so two failures are recorded as only one. This allows reminders to exceed the intended two-failure limit. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths.

findings.title: Do not let failure bookkeeping abort the remaining reminder batch
findings.body: The new workflowReminder.update inside the catch block can itself throw and is not protected. For example, if a reminder is deleted after findMany (by a concurrent cleanup run or workflow deletion), scheduling or the success update can fail, and this catch then attempts to update a nonexistent row. Prisma throws, terminating the handler and leaving every remaining reminder in the batch unprocessed. Previously the catch logged the error and continued. Make the retry update tolerate deleted rows and preserve per-reminder error isolation.
